newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Nedcor set for further income growth.
newsitem.headline: Nedcor set for further income growth.

text.p: South African banking group Nedcor Ltd would see continued earnings growth and maintain the upwardly mobile trend it has enjoyed for the last four years, chief executive Richard Laubscher said on Thursday.
"Despite ongoing difficult trading conditions we would hope the present rate of earnings growth will continue into the future," Laubscher said at a results presentation.
Nedcor could see full year interest income growth of 20 percent if results were adjusted for the new financial service levy (FSL), he said.

Adjusting the interim income statement for the FSL, Laubscher said interest income in the six months to March 31 had grown 20 percent, while the published accounts showed an increase of 16 percent to 1,391 million rand.
"The income statement by year end will be more consistent with this (FSL adjusted)," he said, adding that the growth trend in second half earnings was stronger than the first half.

Furthermore, Nedcor had been conservative in its reporting and so was "quite pleased" with its 24 percent rise in earnings per share amid a an environment of volatile and high money market shortages, Laubscher said.
Nedcor raised earnings per share to 261 cents from 210 cents and hiked its dividend to 56 cents from 45 cents.
Risk provisioning as a percentage of operating profit was 17.9 percent and levels were expected to improve by the end of the year, Laubscher said.
"We've grown fast and believe cautious provisioning is necessary," he said.
Specific and general risk provisions in the first six month amounted to 187 million rand compared to 149 million rand previously.
The group's UAL Merchant Bank had performed very well, contributing 21 percent to Nedcor's overall income.
"It was a very good performance. We're quite excited about the resurgence of UAL," Laubscher said.
He said Nedcor was trying to broaden UAL's interests and had been speaking to possible parties overseas.
